title: Territory routing: permitlist/blocklist failover graph and per-customer overrides for EU-only constraints
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a territory-aware routing policy that enforces EU-only processing by default while supporting tenant-scoped permitlists and blocklists, deterministic failover to safe model variants, and an auditable emergency passthrough path. Deliverables include control-plane policy model, runtime enforcement hooks, API for per-customer overrides, telemetry, and a canary rollout plan.
background: Customers in EU require strict egress and residency guarantees; current coarse-grained geo-routing cannot express per-tenant exceptions or emergency escape semantics.
Existing tickets have explored region routing and residency enforcement but lack a unified failover graph and per-customer override surface that is auditable and reversible.
This work targets a policy primitive that operators and account owners can use to declare territory constraints and opt authorized accounts into limited exceptions under logged conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes a YAML policy schema that supports: account-level permitlist/blocklist, route-level constraints, ordered failover edges to fallback model variants, and emergency passthrough with mandatory audit metadata.
Runtime can evaluate policy in <5ms median added latency per decision at 99th percentile traffic and enforce decisions at model selection time.
Telemetry emits metrics: routed_requests_total, blocked_requests_total, passthrough_audit_count, fallback_invocations by territory and account.
End-to-end canary across 5 customers shows correct routing behavior and full audit trail without data leakage to non-EU egress pools.
Security review and legal signoff completed and documented in Confluence.
implementation_notes: Policy precedence: explicit blocklist > explicit permitlist > route-level constraint > global default. This ensures deny takes precedence when present.
Policy evaluation points: prefer control plane decision cached at request routing layer (short TTL) and validated at runtime when selecting model variant to prevent accidental egress.
Failover graph: model_variant_A (eu-only) -> model_variant_B (eu-compatible quantized variant) -> model_variant_C (metadata-only fallback). Edges encode allowed egress and quality degradation budget.
Per-customer overrides require a signed operator action recorded in audit log with reason, expiration, and operator id. Overrides are stored encrypted and TTL-checked.
Emergency passthrough: can be enabled per-account with constrained routes (no external logging, full redaction options) and triggers automated alerting and post-incident review.
runtime_changes: Add Decision API endpoint in routing service that accepts (account_id, route, headers, consent_flags) and returns (action, target_pool, fallback_chain, audit_token).
Implement policy cache keyed by account_id + route with TTL=30s and reactive invalidation on policy update events.
Instrument model selection path to consult runtime decision and enforce egress checks before opening network connections to non-EU pools.
Introduce soft-fail mode for early canary where violations are logged and counted but requests continue with a flag for operator review.
api_changes: New admin API: POST /v1/policies/territories - create/update policy blobs (YAML) with validation and preview mode.
New admin API: POST /v1/accounts/{id}/overrides - create per-account permit/block entries with operator metadata.
Update public routing API to accept optional 'consent' header that factors into policy decisions for EU egress.
Expose GET /v1/policies/preview?account=... to simulate routing outcome for given sample request.
observability: Logs: structured audit entries for every override and emergency passthrough with operator, timestamp, and request sample id.
Dashboards: per-account routing compliance panel, top accounts by passthroughs, and failover chain heatmap.
Alerts: >0.1% passthrough rate for an account triggers immediate paging to compliance on-call.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and precedence rules with edge cases (overlapping lists, expired overrides).
Integration tests simulating traffic from EU vs non-EU IPs and asserting model pool selection and no external egress for EU-only accounts.
Chaos test: simulate policy-store latency/partial failures and assert soft-fail mode behavior and safe defaults.
Canary plan: 3-stage rollout - preview-only -> soft-fail (log only) -> enforced for canary tenants -> ramp to all.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfiguration could route EU data outside the EU. Mitigation: block-first policy, mandatory dry-run and legal signoff before lift of enforcement for any global change.
Risk: operator overrides abused. Mitigation: require 2-person approval for permanent overrides; short TTL by default and automatic rollback.
Risk: high decision latency. Mitigation: in-process LRU cache at routing layer, optimized evaluation engine in Rust, telemetry to detect hotspots.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: schema + validation in control plane; no runtime enforcement (preview-only).
Stage 1: soft-fail enforcement for internal test tenants; collect telemetry for 72 hours.
Stage 2: enable enforcement for 5 pilot customers with support on-call and manual rollback path.
Stage 3: progressive ramp with monitoring and automated policy health checks; full rollout contingent on zero critical violations for 7 days.
Rollback: disable enforcement flag in control plane and invalidate policy caches globally.
rollback_plan: Global feature flag to turn off territory enforcement immediately.
Automated cache purge and traffic switch to legacy geo-router.
Post-rollback runbook to notify affected customers and start incident review.
